what_this_is: The 2026-09-16 re-audit's central finding is not that individual guards were wrong. It is that guards were written where production does not go. A guard whose reach nobody states is a guard whose reach nobody can lose, so reach is DECLARED here, per guard family, and tools/certification/guard_reach.py refuses a declaration that is not checkable. A status is a declaration about what the code does, not a summary of what a grep found: nothing here is inferred.

statuses.REACHED: a production entry point reaches the rule and a named test exercises it there
statuses.LIBRARY_ONLY: the rule exists and no production entry point reaches it. This is a FINDING and must name the improvement that will close it
statuses.LATENT: the rule guards a shape that does not occur in the tree at all, so there is nothing to reach yet. Not the same as unreached, and must say what would create it

production_entry_points: the domain runners under engcore.domains (thermal_models, electrical.dc, battery, kinetics.cstr, repair)
residuals: This is the REACH map for the guard families whose reach the audit measured by R-xx, not a complete guard inventory. The inventory is tests/mutation_guards.py's job and the Core Freeze V4 round's (I-30).

The four bypass checks are SYNTACTIC. A bypass written in a shape none of them matches -- a dynamic dispatch, a getattr, a call through an alias the checker does not resolve -- is not caught. Each row says per check what it cannot see rather than claiming completeness.
The verifier reads src/engcore only. A bypass in benchmarks/, in a script or in a test is not production and is not checked.

guards.title: A grid rebuild turns an unassessed or incomplete uniqueness search into a SUPPORTED one-mode grid

guards.why: The rule is right and there is nothing in the tree for it to reach: route_uncertainty has no caller in src at all. The one production study reaches the V2 gates through grid_predictive_uncertainty directly (see R-02) rather than through the router, so the rebuild shape does not occur in production today. That is LATENT and not LIBRARY_ONLY: LIBRARY_ONLY would say a production path bypasses the rule, and no production path asks for a rebuild.
guards.what_would_create_it: a production call to engcore.hybrid_uq.router.route_uncertainty. I-13 (binding routed predictions to calibration content) and I-07 (grid evidence the supplier cannot steer) are where a routed production path would arrive; on that day the ROUTE_UNCERTAINTY_REBUILD_WITHOUT_MULTISTART check turns the audited shape -- a rebuild policy passed together with multistart=None, which asks for the rebuild while declining the search -- into a build failure instead of a SUPPORTED one-mode grid.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a rebuild policy reached through a variable the checker cannot resolve (policy = None; ...; route_uncertainty(rebuild=policy, multistart=policy2)), and a caller that passes a multistart argument whose value is a None-valued name rather than the literal None.

guards.title: The production calibration study predicts and validates through frozen V1 functions, so no V2 evidence gate runs
guards.rule_symbol: grid_predictive_uncertainty (CORE-006 route claim and evidence judgement) over grid_goodness_of_fit (CORE-001), grid_containment (CORE-002), require_grid_is_this_evidence (CORE-005) and grid_prior_uniformity (CORE-010)

Residual, stated rather than hidden behind the status: the study is the only production path that predicts at all. bypass_allow_list_reasons.src/engcore/uq/predictive.py: it IS posterior_predictive_uq. The frozen V1 function applies only the grid-resolution refusal, which is exactly why a direct consumer of it is the audited shape.

It does NOT apply grid_goodness_of_fit: a content binding is about whether the grid is THIS posterior's evidence, not about whether the model fits, and the fit statement belongs to the verdict the binding is attached to. That omission is a residual BATCH17's protocol states, and this allow-list entry is where it stays visible.

guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a consumer that reaches the frozen function through an alias (f = posterior_predictive_uq; f(...)), through a getattr, or through a re-export the checker does not resolve back to this name.

guards.title: The CORE-014 operating-point binding never fires in production and is bypassable when enabled
guards.rule_symbol: ScientificModelDefinition.assess_validity(record_values=...) and ValidityAssessment.evaluated, bound by ScientificResult._require_assessment_is_about_this_model and CredibilityEvidenceReport._require_assessments_at_this_operating_point
guards.why: record_values defaults to False on a V1-frozen symbol's method and before batch 14 NOTHING in src passed True, so the CORE-014 binding looped over an empty mapping on every production path. Batch 14 set the default to True on DomainValidityContext.assess -- the domains' own helper, and the path battery, electrical and repair all assess through -- and passed it explicitly at the conduction and KCL sites, so a result or a credibility report now refuses a verdict made at a different operating point than its own provenance states. Residual, recorded on the report rather than hidden: 59 of the 77 condition names across the 16 registered models are reserved DERIVED quantities and 18 are declared inputs, so most names cannot be bound by name at all; they are REPORTED in CredibilityEvidenceReport.unbound_assessment_values and not counted as agreements (D-14-1). An interval verdict binds only the values that did not move within the step, so a coupled battery step binds its state of charge and current and not its temperature.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: an assessment built by hand rather than through assess_validity -- a ValidityAssessment(...) constructor call with an empty `evaluated` -- and an assessment produced outside src/engcore/domains. The first is what the MCP boundary's registry check and the model-id/version binding are for; the second is not production. The check also cannot see a call that passes record_values=False, which is a DECLARATION that the caller does not want the bytes: the shape it finds is a caller who never considered the question.
guards.note_on_the_empty_allow_list: BATCH19's preregistration expected domains/derived_context.py on this allow-list, because its own default is True. It is not needed: that method forwards `record_values=record_values` to assess_validity, so the checker sees the name in the argument list and the site is not a hit. An allow-list entry that is not needed is a hole nobody would notice, so the list is empty and the expectation is recorded as an amendment in the protocol instead.

entry_points: engcore.mcp.tools.run_electrothermal (the cross-solver check emitted when a second route is asked for) -- reaches TrustedConsensusGate, which withholds the level for want of artifact bytes, and then the boundary's own _withhold_level

The production path no longer has such a call at all: the check it emits is the gate's. What no static check can see is a check COPIED from a genuine consensus onto another result -- it carries a genuine threshold record and a genuine basis line -- which needs the check bound to the result it qualifies (CORE-009/VAL-01, I-20's).

guards.title: UncertaintySource never reaches a verdict or report, and SRIA budgets accept NUMERICAL as model-form
guards.rule_symbol: the unattributed-channel refusal in UncertaintyBudget.aggregate; channels_from_predictive_uncertainty with CHANNEL_OF_SOURCE, and require_source_fits_channel with CHANNEL_ACCEPTS_SOURCE, in src/engcore/sria/uncertainty.py; the declared source_kind on the two V1 predictive intervals in src/engcore/uq/predictive.py (batch 8)
guards.closed_by: I-09/I-10 (batch 8) and I-25 part C (batch 54); the remaining half is a PRODUCER no rule can write
guards.why: PARTIAL, and LATENT rather than LIBRARY_ONLY as of batch 54, with the reason stated rather than softened. What is closed: the report carries per-value uncertainty with its source_kind (batch 8), the two V1 predictive intervals declare PARAMETER and COMBINED, a record filed under a channel its own source contradicts is refused at declaration and at the budget, an unattributed quantified record can no longer be AGGREGATED into a total presented as the channels' own -- which is exactly the audited harm, 'the SRIA budget marks aleatoric and model_form known from a numerical-only record' -- and channels_from_predictive_uncertainty carries a declared V1 record onto the channel its own source names, which is the connection batch 8 left missing. What is NOT closed, and cannot be by a rule: no domain solver in this repository quantifies uncertainty at all. Every one emits Uncertainty.unknown with a stated reason, which is the honest state of a solve nobody put an uncertainty budget on, and inventing a number for a channel is the defect this whole round is about. LATENT is therefore the right word for the guards: nothing in src builds an UncertaintyDeclaration, so the shape they guard is not produced in the tree.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The refusal is on the KIND, not on the truth: a caller may declare MEASUREMENT on a discretization estimate and no rule here can tell. What is closed is silence being counted. An unattributed quantified record may still be DECLARED and read -- the pinned harnesses do exactly that, and `unattributed_channels` names it -- because a refusal at declaration time would make a pinned experiment unrunnable rather than making anything more honest. And no rule can produce the missing producer: a domain that does not quantify a channel says so with UNKNOWN, and that silence stays visible rather than being filled in.
guards.what_would_create_it: A caller building an UncertaintyDeclaration from a production record -- which channels_from_predictive_uncertainty now exists for -- or a domain solver that actually quantifies a channel. The audited shapes are a quantified record whose source_kind is UNSPECIFIED being counted as a channel's known uncertainty and combined into a total, and a record filed under a channel its own source contradicts. The SHA-256-pinned E1 and E2 experiment harnesses file unattributed quantified records under channels today, which is why the refusal is at aggregation rather than at declaration (batch 54's amendments 1 and 2).

guards.title: Cross-domain crossings carry bare point values, and UncertaintyTransfer binds nothing
guards.rule_symbol: UncertaintyTransfer, which binds a crossing quantity's propagated uncertainty to the transfer that produced it; the interval-containment, attribution, chain-meeting and completeness rules of part B (_require_the_interval_contains_the_value, _require_the_uncertainty_names_the_source, the value-meeting refusal in propagate_uncertainty_chain, _completeness_of and the attribution that keeps both references), with EnergyConversion.efficiency_uncertainty; CrossedQuantity and CrossedQuantity.from_result (part C), with CoupledRun.crossings and recorded_crossings in src/engcore/systems/electrothermal/coupled.py
guards.closed_by: I-27 parts A, B and C (batches 47, 48 and 49)
guards.why: The problem is REACHED in production -- the audit's own value, and why this row's audit_reached_in_production is `yes` -- while the GUARD is not. The production electrothermal coupling passes bare point values across the thermal/electrical boundary with no uncertainty, no validity state and no validation state attached, and UncertaintyTransfer, the record that would bind them, has no caller in src. So a crossing that loses its uncertainty loses it silently: the receiving domain sees a number, and nothing downstream can tell a propagated quantity from a declared one. This is the one row where LIBRARY_ONLY understates the risk rather than overstating it, because the unguarded path is the one production actually runs. I-27 is where the transfers carry uncertainty and validity with physically bound checks. Part B (batch 48) closed everything the record itself can answer: an INTERVAL must contain the value it is about, an attribution must name something the crossing names, the propagated record keeps BOTH provenances, a chain propagates only where consecutive values meet, and a conversion whose efficiency declares no uncertainty says structurally that the width is a lower bound. The STATUS is unchanged and is the finding: nothing in src/ calls this module yet, so every production crossing still carries a bare point value. That is part C, and it is what will move this row to REACHED. Part C (batch 49) closed the production half and is what moves this row: the fixed-point electrothermal loop now records one CrossedQuantity per crossing, carrying the producing result's own uncertainty entry for the quantity, its per-model applicability verdicts, its validation status and its convergence state -- every one of them read OFF that result by from_result rather than taken from a caller. So the guard family has a production caller, which is exactly what LIBRARY_ONLY said it did not.
entry_points: engcore.domains.battery.coupling (the coupled step) -- still crosses values through its own step and builds no QuantityTransfer records at all, so there is nothing yet to attach a crossing to; named here as the remaining production path rather than counted as reached
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: nothing static: a crossing that passes a float is a call the checker could find only by knowing which arguments are crossing quantities, which is a type question and not a syntactic one. I-27's own tests are what will measure it once the transfers exist; until then this row is the declaration that they do not. As of part B: the attribution rule is a containment test over what the crossing names, so it refuses an uncertainty bound to nothing and does not verify that the named result's own uncertainty entry for that quantity IS this one -- that needs the result passed in, which is part C's business where it builds the transfers. Quadrature assumes the efficiency's uncertainty is independent of the input's, and that assumption is RECORDED in the propagated method and notes rather than established. An INTERVAL under a conversion is never combined with an efficiency uncertainty, because a bound and a standard uncertainty need a distribution nobody declared; the record says lower bound instead. As of part C: production writes Uncertainty.unknown with a stated reason on every metric it reports, so what crosses is an UNKNOWN carrying that reason. This makes the producing side's silence VISIBLE at the crossing; it quantifies nothing, and no rule here could. The battery coupling is untouched for the reason in the entry points. The crossing carries the source's validation STATUS and convergence state rather than its whole report, because the report is on the result the crossing names and a copy would be a second place for it to be edited. And mcp/evidence.py does not render the crossings: what a report shows is a decision per consumer.

guards.title: Quantity.parse evaluates unit expressions, magnitudes accept bool or str, and delta units pass as absolute
guards.rule_symbol: Quantity.parse and Quantity.__post_init__ over _declared_magnitude, _require_the_unit_is_a_unit_and_not_arithmetic, _require_the_magnitude_written_is_the_magnitude_parsed and is_delta_unit; the delta refusal itself is src/engcore/mcp/problem.py::_read_quantity
guards.why: Every declared value in an MCP run_electrothermal or run_battery payload is read by _read_quantity, which calls Quantity.parse and now also refuses a delta unit where the binding's unit_exemplar is absolute. The reproductions run through build_electrothermal_problems on the SHIPPED example payload rather than through the parser alone, which is what makes the row REACHED rather than LIBRARY_ONLY. Residual, stated rather than hidden behind the status: the grammar is about TEXT, so a caller constructing Quantity(5.0, 'volt') in process bypasses it entirely -- as it must, that being the two-argument path the class is built on -- and only __post_init__'s bool/str rule reaches there. The library comparisons that also mishandle offset scales (R-48, R-52, R-57) are parts B and C of this improvement and are LIBRARY_ONLY until then.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a boundary other than _read_quantity that reads a declared unit and checks only its dimension. The delta rule is applied at one call site, not enforced structurally, so a second such reader would have to consult is_delta_unit itself -- which is why parts B and C put the rule into the library comparisons rather than leaving it at the boundary.

guards.title: The consensus verdict depends on route order through the first route's unit
guards.rule_symbol: CrossSolverConsensus.from_results' canonical common_unit (base_unit of each quantity's dimension) and its is_ratio_scale refusal, over _compare, relative_difference and _floored_difference; the same rule in src/engcore/scientific/oracles.py::_same_operating_point
guards.why: LATENT rather than REACHED, and the distinction is the point of this ledger. Both rules sit on code production runs -- the only production caller of from_results is engcore.domains.electrical.dc_consensus, and _same_operating_point is read by ScientificResult's CORE-009/CORE-014 validity binding -- but neither production path can currently present the SHAPE the rules are about. DC lists the native route first and reports on volt and ampere, both coherent SI units, so the canonical conversion is the identity and no recorded magnitude or digest moves; no production result states an operating point on an offset scale. So the fix is real and the guards are exercised, in the library, by the tests below. Claiming REACHED would be claiming a production exercise that does not exist, which is the assertion I-16 was written to stop.
guards.what_would_create_it: A second caller of CrossSolverConsensus.from_results whose routes report one name in different units of the same dimension -- which is the ordinary case the moment an external provider reports in its own units rather than the native route's -- or any production result that states an operating point on an offset temperature scale, degC being the unit an engineer writes.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: CrossSolverConsensus.over, which takes bare numbers and has no units to canonicalise. It cannot award CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED (IND-02), so what it records is a measurement rather than a claim -- but a caller reading its worst relative difference is reading whatever scale it handed in.

guards.title: The corner-agreement guard compares magnitudes in each law's own unit
guards.rule_symbol: _require_corners_agree, over CORNER_AGREEMENT_REL_TOL: both meeting laws' magnitudes converted into base_unit(definition.unit) before the difference is taken
guards.why: LATENT rather than REACHED. require_complete_boundary IS reached -- the conduction2d domain calls it -- but no shipped 2D declaration states two edges of one field in different units of the same dimension: they state kelvin throughout, so the conversion is the identity and the guard's behaviour on production declarations is unchanged. The guard is nevertheless the production refusal, and the audit records what its absence cost: in conduction2d the corner node is pinned to whichever edge the assembly writes last and the domain's own boundary_conditions_held check reports FAIL -- a contradiction found after the solve rather than refused before it, and found only because that domain happens to check. A consumer relying on the core refusal got nothing.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any declaration that states one field's edges in more than one unit of its dimension -- a plate whose ambient side is given in degC and whose heated side in kelvin, which is how an engineer would write it -- or a field declared in degC, whose corner agreement was judged on a scale whose zero is a convention.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: Two edges that agree at every corner and disagree along a shared span. They cannot share a span on a structured quadrilateral, so there is nothing more to compare here -- but that is a property of this support type, not a general one.

guards.title: Spreads on offset temperature scales convert as absolute temperatures
guards.rule_symbol: require_spread_unit and Quantity.magnitude_as_spread_in over _slope_against_base, plus Quantity.to's wrapping of a backend scale refusal; applied at every declared spread in the core -- OracleObservation.absolute_tolerance, ConstraintDefinition.tolerance and the margin its check reports, GaussianObservation.sigma as read by ObservationSet.numeric_vectors and by inference/split.py's two content digests, and PredictiveObservableSpec.observation_sigma
guards.closed_by: I-22 parts D (batch 29, the audit's finding 58) and E (batch 30, finding 99)
guards.why: FIXED, in two batches. R-48 is one defect at four sites and every site needed a conversion the units module did not have: a difference transforms by the linear part of an affine map, and `magnitude_in` applies the whole map. Part D gave the module `magnitude_as_spread_in` and `require_spread_unit`, wrapped the backend's scale refusal in this package's own error, and fixed the oracle tolerance. Part E applied both primitives at every other DECLARED spread, which is what part D's own version of this row named as the reason it stayed PARTIAL: `require_spread_unit` is applied at call sites, and nothing structurally requires a spread field to consult it. Now every spread field in `src/engcore` does. LATENT rather than REACHED: `ConstraintDefinition` is reached by every MCP rating and limit check, `GaussianObservation` by the production calibration study and by `studies/tcr`, `PredictiveObservableSpec` by the predictive layer the study routes through -- and all of them are reached with RATIO-SCALE units, ohm, watt, kelvin, ampere, so every conversion is the identity and no production number moves. What is reached is the guard; what is latent is the offset-scale declaration that would trip it.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any declaration that states a tolerance, a sigma or a band on an offset temperature scale -- '2 degC' as a limit tolerance and '0.5 degC' as a measurement sigma are how an engineer and a lab respectively write them, and the first let a 600 kelvin reading satisfy a 358.15 kelvin limit while the second gave a 50 kelvin misfit a chi-squared of 0.033. Or any field, bound or observable declared on an offset scale, where an absolute unit cannot carry the spread or the margin at all.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.problem (rating and limit checks, via ConstraintDefinition.check)
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A spread read with `magnitude_in` DOWNSTREAM of a declaration. `studies/calibration_study.py`, `studies/tcr.py`, `adequacy/predictive.py`, `hybrid_uq/predictive.py` and `uq/predictive.py` do so at several points; those reads are safe because the declaration guard admits only ratio-scale units, where the two readers agree exactly -- but they are safe BY that guard and not by their own statement. And a `Quantity` handed around loose still carries no statement of whether it is a point or a span: what this improvement adds is that every declared spread FIELD makes that statement at construction.

guards.title: A posterior cut at the declared upper bound, with data bounding only the lower side, is SUPPORTED
guards.rule_symbol: _rebuild_grid's per-side bound-domination test over _GAUSSIAN_BAND_SD = sqrt(2 * EDGE_LOG_LIKELIHOOD_DROP), beside the existing both-sides rule; and src/engcore/hybrid_uq/local_gaussian.py::_clamp_leverage_cumulant, the I-14 part that had to land first
guards.closed_by: I-06 (batch 31); the batch also closes I-15's last open conformance case
guards.why: LATENT. The rebuild path is reached only by a caller that supplies both a MultistartPolicy and a table builder: the production calibration study routes a SUPPLIED grid and the MCP tools form no predictive interval at all, so no production path can present the shape. The rule is nevertheless fixed in the router because that is where the width a claim reports is decided. What this closes is the width a SUPPORTED claim WOULD report if such a caller arrived -- 2.372, 2.788 and 3.522 for one set of data at declared upper bounds of 40, 60 and 80. Note that the leverage-null clamp shipped in the same batch IS on every local route, production included; it is carried on I-14's row when that lands, and is recorded here because R-11 could not be exercised at all without it.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that rebuilds a grid from a local covariance -- the documented way to get a posterior when the supplied grid is refused -- on a problem where the data constrain a parameter from one side only. A decay rate whose signal is gone inside the observation window is the ordinary case: every rate above some value predicts the same thing, so the upper side is whatever was declared.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The refinement regime, and deliberately. A posterior the data HAVE localised but which a declared bound truncates still reports a width that depends on where the bound is -- 0.6712, 0.8912, 1.129, 1.341 and 1.699 at bounds of 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16 -- because the moments of a truncated distribution do depend on the truncation, and the audit's own fix direction asks for that path to be kept. The line between the two regimes is the 5.2565 sd band distance and it is drawn on purpose; BATCH31_THRESHOLD_PROTOCOL.json states both sequences so the choice is visible.

guards.title: An evidence-binding mismatch raises instead of passing over
guards.rule_symbol: grid_is_this_evidence (returns) beside require_grid_is_this_evidence (raises), and the router's supplied-grid path consulting the first
guards.why: LATENT. The production calibration study supplies a grid it built itself in the same process, so the binding it faces is its own and cannot disagree; the MCP tools supply no grid. The rule is nevertheless what decides whether a request survives a fact about its grid, which is why it is fixed at the router and not left to a caller's try/except.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that supplies a grid a DIFFERENT process computed -- which is what supplying a grid is for. A solver converged to 1e-9 relative against observations with sigma 1e-4 relative is enough: that is about 1e-5 of a sigma per residual, ten times the 1e-6 the binding allows, and it aborted the whole request.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: Which NODES the binding re-evaluates, and that the supplier chooses them. R-19 is I-07 part B and is OPEN: a supplier who keeps the checked rows honest can still sharpen the posterior bulk, and now gets PASSED_OVER rather than a raise when caught -- which is this part working, not a weakening of that one.

guards.title: The uniform-prior step tolerance refuses a grid that is effectively uniform
guards.rule_symbol: grid_prior_uniformity's moment-effect bound over _reweighted_moment_shift and PRIOR_REWEIGHT_MOMENT_SD
guards.why: LATENT, and this row is about a claim newly ALLOWED rather than newly refused, which is the direction this round is normally careful about. No production path supplies a grid on an axis whose spelling disagrees with its declared transform, so nothing production does changes. The bound is measured rather than assumed, and the detail records how far the moments actually moved.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that supplies a grid spaced in natural units for a LOG-declared parameter -- which is what `numpy.linspace` gives you, and is how the audited case arose. Its prior density varied about 4% and its moments matched the accepted spelling's to six digits.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The reweighting's effect on the FIRST TWO moments of each axis marginal. A node density that leaves both alone and distorts a tail, or a correlation, is not caught. The first two moments are what a grid route REPORTS, so they are what the rule is about -- but this is not a statement that the prior is uniform.

guards.title: Evidence binding spot-checks 8 nodes, 4 of them seeded from the supplier's bytes
guards.rule_symbol: _spot_check_rows over SPOT_CHECK_WEIGHTED_ROWS and SPOT_CHECK_INADMISSIBLE_ROWS, with a verifier-side nonce and every face's highest node; the same rule in src/engcore/hybrid_uq/router.py::_require_table_agrees_with_forward
guards.why: LATENT. The production calibration study supplies a grid it built itself in the same process, so the binding it faces is its own and there is no supplier to be adversarial; the MCP tools supply no grid. The threat the rule is about is a grid computed elsewhere, which is what supplying a grid is FOR -- so this is the guard on the feature rather than on a current caller.
guards.what_would_create_it: The first caller that supplies a grid, or a rebuild table_builder, that another party computed. The audited forgery needed no privileged access: keep the four fixed rows honest, sharpen the bulk, and nudge one far-tail log-likelihood by 1e-9 until the four seeded rows miss it. Two attempts, and the result was GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED with every reported width halved.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A tampered region holding LESS than a quarter of the posterior weight: 17 weighted draws catch a 10% region about 83% of the time, not 99%. The rule states a detection probability against a stated fraction and claims no more; certainty needs the audit's other alternative, re-evaluating every node within ln 1e6 of the peak, at a cost proportional to the grid. And the weighted draw uses the GRID's own weights, so a forger who lowers the weight of what they tampered with reduces their chance of being drawn -- but that lowering is itself the tampering and moves the moments the route reports, which is what the honest-versus-forged comparison measures. guards.rule_symbol: the bare-string refusal in CategoryCondition.__post_init__ (and the unconverted payload in from_dict); the denominator-sign UNKNOWN in CrossLimitCondition.evaluate_in with UnknownReason.RELATION_NOT_ORDERED_BY_THE_DECLARATION, its guidance in engcore/domains/repair.py and its cause in unknown_diagnostics
guards.why: LATENT: both rules sit on constructors and an evaluator that production does run, and neither shape occurs in the tree. No in-tree declaration passes a bare string for an allowed set -- every one passes a tuple -- and every in-tree cross-limit operand is an absolute temperature in kelvin, which is positive by construction. That is why the audit had to build both cases by hand.
guards.what_would_create_it: A declaration written with `allowed='laminar'` instead of `allowed=('laminar',)`, which is a plausible slip because the string is iterable and the constructor accepted it; or a cross-limit condition over a sign-indefinite dimension -- a voltage, a charge, a signed power flow -- where the denominator can go negative and the ratio bound stops ordering its operands.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A CategoryCondition still accepts any other iterable of strings, so a caller who passes a list of words gets the set they meant; what is refused is the one shape whose meaning inverts silently. The sign rule is on the DENOMINATOR alone (amendment 1), because with b > 0 the ratio orders a and b for a of either sign -- so a condition over a sign-indefinite dimension whose denominator stays positive is assessed as before. A dimension whose operands both go negative cannot be ratio-bounded by this record at all: it returns UNKNOWN with its own reason rather than pretending to order them, and expressing 'a <= b' without a ratio is a different record.

guards.title: Oracle operating-point conditions are the caller's word, partial and optional
guards.rule_symbol: OracleEvidenceSet._binding_gap and the predicted_from keyword of OracleEvidenceSet.compare; the stated-but-undeclared refusal and the undeclared-point level withholding inside compare
guards.closed_by: I-26 (batch 51); the REACH is a repository decision about pinning an oracle, not an improvement
guards.why: LATENT, and the audit's own word for the problem -- 'library-only' -- is kept in the field above. LATENT is the ledger's category for a rule whose shape does not occur in the tree at all, which is this one: the oracle comparison is the designed route to EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED and BENCHMARK_VALIDATED, and no production path reaches it because `_TRUSTED_ORACLE_DECLARATIONS` is empty and nothing outside the core builds an evidence set. The rules themselves are closed: a level now requires the prediction to name the record it was computed from, whose own inputs must be the stated point and whose values must be the compared numbers; a stated condition the evidence does not describe stops that comparison; and evidence that declares no point is compared and awards no level.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: `predicted_from` is optional, so a caller may still compare a bare mapping -- what that caller cannot do is earn a level from it, which is the claim the finding is about. Making the record mandatory is a signature change the compatibility rule forbids before the V4 round. When a record IS named, the binding is that it carries these values and that its own provenance inputs are the stated point, so a result that does not declare its operating point cannot support a level either -- an absence this reports rather than infers. Oracle authority is unchanged and is the ceiling on all of this: `_TRUSTED_ORACLE_DECLARATIONS` is empty, nothing outside the core builds an OracleEvidenceSet, and no oracle is pinned, so no production path awards an oracle level at all. Pinning one is a repository decision about external evidence, not something a rule can close. `_same_operating_point` is reused unchanged, so its offset-scale behaviour (the audit's finding 104) applies here too and belongs to another problem.
guards.what_would_create_it: An oracle pinned in `_TRUSTED_ORACLE_DECLARATIONS` together with an `OracleProvider` that builds an `OracleEvidenceSet` for a problem -- which is what the route to EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED and BENCHMARK_VALIDATED is designed to be, and what no path in this repository does today. Until then no comparison of a real prediction against external evidence exists to reach: the shapes these rules guard (a bare mapping asserted to be at an operating point, a two-point dataset, a prediction missing a metric) occur only in tests.

guards.title: Field validity decides from an unbound self-declared summary and a component envelope
guards.rule_symbol: FieldSummary's self-consistency rules and magnitude_maximum; FieldRecord's dimension and count checks, summary_verified_against and summary_is_bound_to_its_values; FieldValue._require_the_summary_describes_these_values and _magnitude_maximum in src/engcore/data/field.py; the binding and magnitude branches of FieldRangeCondition.evaluate and FieldFiniteCondition.evaluate in src/engcore/scientific/models/structured_validity.py
guards.closed_by: I-25 part A (batch 52); part B is R-63 and R-73
guards.why: LATENT for the PREDICATES, which is what the problem is about: FieldRangeCondition and FieldFiniteCondition are registered validity-condition decoders and are therefore reachable from a payload, and no production domain declares one -- the audit says so in its own words, 'no production domain uses these conditions yet'. The summary rules themselves sit on records production DOES produce, so a field stored by the conduction2d path now carries the digest of the bytes its summary came from, and a summary that disagrees with those bytes is refused on read.
guards.what_would_create_it: A domain declaring a FieldRangeCondition or a FieldFiniteCondition over a field it produces -- which is what the structured-validity decoders exist for -- or any consumer reading a field record's summary and acting on it without resolving the bytes. The audited shapes are a summary nobody derived from its own field (a 900 K hot spot summarized as 310 K with the reference digest unchanged) and a multi-component field judged per component ((1, 1, 1) m/s passing a 1.2 m/s bound).
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The verification digest is an integrity binding, as every digest here is: it closes an unbound summary and a silent hand-off, not a determined edit by somebody who recomputes the digest too. `from_record` can only check what it resolves, so the reader this record exists for -- one that acts on the summary WITHOUT resolving a mesh-sized array -- is protected by the digest binding and the internal consistency rules rather than by a re-derivation it never performs. `magnitude_maximum` is a maximum only, because a minimum magnitude is not a bound anybody writes for a vector field; a condition stating only a minimum over a multi-component field therefore answers UNKNOWN. The per-component envelope stays on the record, because a component-wise bound is a legitimate statement -- what changed is which one the condition applies.

guards.title: FieldTransferContract accepts any verdict
guards.rule_symbol: FieldTransferContract._require_the_verdict_follows_from_the_records and the _STRENGTH ordering it compares against
guards.why: LATENT, and the audit's own word for it. No `src` consumer builds a FieldTransferContract: the record exists to be the gate a field crossing passes, and the crossing does not exist yet. The rule is closed: the contract carries both field definitions and both support fingerprints -- which is what check_field_transfer decides from -- and it now refuses a verdict that claims more crossability than those records permit, while a more conservative verdict stays allowed.
guards.what_would_create_it: A field dependency actually crossing between two problems, which is what FieldDependency and check_field_transfer are for and what NEEDS.md's field-transfer milestone describes. The audited shapes are a payload computed as REFUSED for 1 component against 3 or kelvin against pascal reading back as COMPATIBLE, and direct construction with invented fingerprints.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: Geometry beyond fingerprint equality: two supports covering different rectangles and two resolutions of one rectangle both appear on the record as two different fingerprints, so a REFUSED-for-geometry verdict is indistinguishable from a REQUIRES_PROJECTION-for-resolution one without the meshes. The contract therefore refuses a verdict that claims too much and does not re-derive WHICH reason a refusal rests on. A conservative verdict is deliberately left constructible, because a caller may refuse for a reason the record does not carry and this record must stay able to say so.

guards.title: FieldObservationOperator binds its region by label and snaps out-of-support probes to an edge
guards.rule_symbol: FieldObservationOperator.region_mesh_id and .region_edge with _require_the_region_is_the_declared_one, _require_the_probe_is_on_the_support with PROBE_CONTAINMENT_RTOL, and _values_of_the_field_it_names
guards.why: LATENT, and the audit's own word for it: the operator is reached from tests and benchmarks and from no production path -- no domain builds a field observation for a calibration yet. The rules are closed: the region's content (its support and its edge) is declared, is in the canonical form and therefore in the digest, and a region whose content differs is refused; a probe outside the support's rectangle is refused instead of being answered with a corner node; and a typed field handed to apply must be the field the operator names, in its dimension, on its support.
guards.what_would_create_it: A calibration that observes a solved field -- the thing this module is the spike for: a probe or an edge mean entering an inference problem as an observation. The audited shapes are two MeshRegion objects sharing a region id and differing in edge (the left edge at 400 K and the right at 300 K under one digest), a probe declared 2 m and -5 m from a 10 mm plate, and a bare float array whose unit and field id the operator asserted.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: MeshRegion still binds its own mesh by `mesh_id`, which is a label two discretisations of one geometry share; putting a fingerprint on the region is a change to that record and is not this batch's. Containment is checked against the support's rectangle and not against the cell the probe falls in, so a probe inside the rectangle that snaps half a cell is still answered and `probe_offset` remains the only place that says so -- refusing there would delete every legitimate coarse-mesh probe. And `apply` still accepts a bare sequence, where the unit and the field id stay the caller's assertion; making the typed field mandatory is a signature change the compatibility rule forbids before the V4 round.

guards.title: The round's batch-guard mutation evidence sat outside the pinned harness and any failure counted as a kill
guards.rule_symbol: POPULATION_V4 (563 entries), with tools/certification/mutation_v4_runner.py::verdict_from_junit and require_an_isolated_tree, and tests/test_mutation_population_v4.py as the FAST-tier check that each entry still matches
guards.why: REACHED, and by the only kind of production this rule has: the certification control plane. The population is DATA inside the area `tools/certification/core_certificate.py` pins and digests, the runner is the module the recertify workflow invokes, and the FAST-tier suite applies all 563 entries to the live source on every run. What the audit measured -- 55 scripts under benchmarks/ that nothing verified, two kills that no longer applied, and a runner crediting any non-zero exit -- is closed: 25 moved entries are repointed with their reasons, 2 that cannot be applied are marked and never applied, and a kill is the ONE test the entry names failing in that run's JUnit report.
entry_points: tools/certification/mutation_v4_runner.py::main (the shard runner the recertify workflow invokes)
tools/certification/core_certificate.py::build_manifest (digests the population as part of the harness area)
tools/certification/mutation_population.py::v4_population (re-derives the population's identity from the tree)
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: That an entry matching exactly once is a KILL. Only the formal round establishes that, and until its transcripts are recorded the FAST check says the population still describes the tree and nothing more. The batch scripts under benchmarks/ remain unpinned by decision: they are the historical record of how each batch ran, and the population is what is verified from now on -- so an edit to a batch script is no longer an edit to any evidence, which is the point, but also means nothing detects one.

guards.title: The certificate harness area did not pin the helper modules its suites import
guards.rule_symbol: harness_import_closure and harness_pinning_problems, called from build_manifest
guards.why: REACHED: the closure is derived and enforced where a certificate is BUILT, so a manifest is refused rather than written over a harness area that does not cover what its own suites read. The finding was that the area was a hand-maintained list -- hybrid_synthetic.py was imported by ten certified targets and measured by nothing, and the branch changed it by twelve lines without moving the certificate -- so the fix is the derivation, not a longer list. The area now enumerates 123 files, and the check compares it against the closure of the harness TARGETS and every target test the V4 population names.
entry_points: tools/certification/core_certificate.py::build_manifest (refuses a scope that does not cover the closure)
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The closure follows STATIC imports. A helper reached only through `importlib` by a computed name, or through a conftest fixture that loads a file by path, is not found -- nothing in the closure does either today, and the check reports what it measured rather than claiming a reach it does not have.

guards.title: The V2 and V3 freeze verifiers accept a self-asserted assurance record
guards.rule_symbol: v4_population (population_sha256 over the ordered ids, definitions_sha256 over the canonical JSON of the full entries) and v4_log_problems (verdicts re-derived from the transcript)
guards.closed_by: I-30 (batch 55) for the population half; I-29 (batch 56) for the freeze record's commit and figures
guards.why: PARTIAL on purpose, and the split is recorded in BATCH55_THRESHOLD_PROTOCOL.json rather than left to a reader. The population half is closed and REACHED: a V4 population's identity is recomputed from the tree, never read from a record, and the digest covers the mutation BODIES so the same ids with a rewritten target test or expectation are a different population; a shard's verdicts are re-derived from its own transcript and each must equal what the ENTRY declares. The other half of finding 91 -- a verifier that re-derives the evidence digests, the measured commit and the figures a certificate asserts, as V1 did -- is the Core Freeze V4 control plane in batch 56.
entry_points: tools/certification/mutation_population.py::main (identity, select and record, invoked per shard by the recertify workflow)
tools/certification/mutation_v4_runner.py::main (reads the population through v4_population and v4_entries)
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A transcript that was never produced by a run. The digests prove WHICH population a shard claims and the lines prove what it reported, and nothing here proves the lines came from executing anything -- that is what the certificate's own commit binding and the fresh-execution gate in the workflow are for, and it is the half batch 56 takes on.
